subject: ventures/chant-forge
professional: a working electronic/metal music producer with a chant-literate choirmaster (a Gregorian schola director) and a mastering engineer: the producer checks that the MIDI and stems drop into a DAW and sit on a grid, the schola director checks the neumes, modes and Latin against the Vatican Graduale, the mastering engineer checks LUFS and true peak against BS.1770 and a distributor's delivery spec

evidence.correctness: Ran: node cli.mjs examples/dies-irae-incipit.gabc --bpm 124 and parsed the MIDI with my own raw-byte Python SMF reader (mido is not installed). By hand from the GABC clef rule (c4 = do on line 4, letter j; f is letter index 5, so 4 steps below do = fa an octave down) f,e,d,c map to MIDI 53,52,50,48; the file holds 53,52,53,50,52,48,50,50 (F E F D E C D D) as expected. The punctum mora d. lasts 480 ticks (2 pulses at 240/pulse, PPQ 480). The tempo meta 0x07621F = 483871 us/beat = 124.0 BPM. The reported 1.38 bars equals (9 note pulses + 2 for the ':' bar rest) = 11 pulses = 5.5 beats = 1.375 bars. Second source: ffmpeg 6.1 ebur128 on a rendered, 191 s Dies irae deep-house preview (not one of the author's synthetic signals): master-cli says -16.6 LUFS, -1.01 dBTP; ffmpeg says I -16.6 LUFS, peak -1.0 dBFS. Third: release.mjs gtinOk against published GS1 examples: 036000291452 true, 4006381333931 true, last digit changed in each: false; isrcOk accepts US-S1Z-99-00001 and rejects a 13-char code. No output was wrong. Not checked (no scans or singers here): the corpus notes against the printed Graduale, so the correctness of the chant itself rests on GregoBase transcribers.
evidence.completeness: Ran the node CLIs for each README 'works now' item I could reach: GABC to MIDI with --fit, --final, --drone, --genre (deep-house, metal accepted; 'deephouse' correctly rejected with the list of names), --suggest-final tests, render-cli WAV (191 s in a few seconds), master-cli (exit and FAIL/PASS lines as documented), release-cli covered by 7 passing tests, --stretch/--halftime/--repeat/--intro/--markers/--lrc/--cues each have passing tests. 59 files exist in corpus/gregobase-1908 as claimed. The README itself says stages 3 (arrange, only MIDI templates), 4 (voice) are not built or not heard and that nothing has been listened to, so the product is a toolchain slice, not a track; every claim of 'done' that I checked worked. I did not run the Playwright browser check (eval/browser-e2e.mjs) or open index.html; the page claims rest on its test file and the author's run.
evidence.verification: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' in ventures/chant-forge: 83 tests, 83 pass, 0 fail, 59 s. Mutation 1: in gabc.mjs changed the 'la' degree from 9 to 10 semitones; chant-forge.test.mjs, batch.test.mjs and real-files.test.mjs then failed 3 tests (caught); reverted. Mutation 2: in master.mjs integratedLufs changed the relative gate from -10 LU to -20 LU (BS.1770 requires -10); master.test.mjs still passed 8/8 (NOT caught), reverted. The unit tests only exercise sines and a clipped file, so the gating that makes the loudness number correct on real music is covered only by eval/ffmpeg-check.mjs, which is a manual script outside the test suite. Fuzz test and a mido read-back are real strengths, but a shipped metric with an untested core branch caps this at 2.
evidence.craft: Read gabc.mjs, midi.mjs, master.mjs (integratedLufs, truePeak), release.mjs (isrc/gtin), cli.mjs and index.html head. Zero dependencies, ES modules, browser-safe (Buffer removed, tested with Buffer deleted), small focused files (gabc 305 lines, genre 170, render 297), clear comments that state limits, deterministic output. Defects: parseGabc is a regex pipeline that drops everything after the first '|' (NABC) and silently skips unknown characters (documented in its header, but no warning is emitted); the true-peak filter is a Hann-windowed sinc, not the Annex 2 coefficients (disclosed in README); the genre warning for BPM is only a warning. No dead code or copied engines found in the files read.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'Tests: 8 tests' in README for chant-forge.test.mjs is stale (13 test() calls in that file now; 83 across the suite); llms.txt, which is the file an LLM is told to trust, still says 'Run only on small test inputs (8 unit tests); not yet tried on real GregoBase or Gregorio files' and 'No genre arrangements, voices, mastering or release tooling yet', all contradicted by README and the repo (59 real files, genre.mjs, master.mjs, release.mjs). README claims about -14 LUFS, true peak, 83 tests, the five corpus pieces, 59 batch files, ffmpeg agreement (reproduced here on a different signal) and 'nobody has listened' are backed by files and honest. Per-service loudness targets are marked 'from memory, verify'. index.html states the preview is a plain synthesiser and that rights must be checked, but I found no explicit not-advice or usage-tracking element in the page source. The relative link RECORDING-GUIDE.md on the page points at a Markdown file; I did not verify the published site serves it.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a producer who wants a chant line in a DAW: paste or load GABC, pick a final inside E2-E4, get a MIDI with lyric events plus a cue sheet and stems, and a master check; that works end to end and is faster than hand-entering notes. Where a producer would stall within the first hour: chant has no metre, and the converter makes every note one eighth pulse with mora and episema as flat multipliers and padding at bars (disclosed), so the line is rhythmically stiff, with no neume-shape nuance (quilisma, liquescent) and nothing heard by a human yet; the first-hour question 'does it sound good' is unanswered by the project itself. The distributable result (an EP) does not exist, and the singing voice stage is not built.
evidence.domain: Compared to Gregorio/GABC semantics, the Solesmes rhythmic reading (notes of roughly equal value, lengthened by mora and episema) and BS.1770-4 / EBU R128. The note-to-pitch mapping, clef rule, flat clef cb, accidentals lasting to the word end or bar, and the mode-final check are faithful to GABC and to the modal system (modes 1-2 on re etc.), and the 11 off-final introits and alleluias are correctly explained by psalm-tone differentiae. Departures a schola director would flag: fixed 4/4 grid fit and half-time doubling alter chant phrasing by design; neume shapes are flattened; the E2-E4 'men's unison range' is the author's guess, not checked with singers; Te Deum and Salve Regina come from 1974 and 1961 books, not pre-1929, despite the public-domain-only rule (disclosed in corpus/README.md, and a licensing risk for any release of those pieces). Loudness work meets a mastering engineer's expectations except the true-peak filter and the missing EBU test files.

defects.what: Mutating the BS.1770 relative gate from -10 LU to -20 LU is not caught by any test in master.test.mjs; the gating that makes the headline LUFS number right on real music is only checked by the manual eval/ffmpeg-check.mjs script.

llms.txt tells an LLM that the project has 8 unit tests, no genre arrangements, mastering or release tooling and has not been run on real files; all are false now (83 tests, genre.mjs, master.mjs, release.mjs, 59 real files).

The corpus includes the Te Deum (Solesmes 1974) and Salve Regina (Liber Usualis 1961), which conflict with the project's own public-domain-before-1929 source rule; disclosed in corpus/README.md but they are still in the studio's sample list and could slip into a release.
README states chant-forge.test.mjs has 8 tests; it now has 13.
Unknown GABC characters are skipped silently with no warning, so a misread neume yields a quiet wrong output rather than a message.
No usage tracking or not-advice disclaimer found in the studio page source despite the repository's new-surface rule.

verdict: Chant Forge is a correct, honest and unusually well-disclosed pipeline slice: every output I recomputed matched (pitches and MIDI timing by hand from the GABC clef rule, loudness and true peak against ffmpeg ebur128 on a rendered real piece, GTIN/ISRC check digits against GS1 examples), 83 of 83 tests pass, and the README says plainly that nothing has been listened to. It does not meet the bar: a seeded bug in the pitch table was caught by 3 tests, but a seeded bug in the loudness relative gate was not caught by any, llms.txt is badly stale and contradicts the README, and a producer or schola director would stall on the stiff fixed-pulse rhythm, flattened neumes, post-1929 corpus entries and the absence of any audio a human has judged. Scores before any fix; the cheapest fixes are a gate test using a loud/quiet signal and rewriting llms.txt Limits from the README.
